mattj: Heads-up — saw an odd KV reuse pattern on prod that looks like 'ghost' prefixes causing reuse misses and steady mem growth in long chat sessions. hit-rate falls after ~18k tokens and kv-page-alloc climbs.
leah: Can you share the profiler output? which symbols are hot?
mattj: flamegraph points at kv_page_alloc, page_compact_scan, and memcpy in page rewrite. the interesting bit: many small allocations with partially-filled pages that never compact. suspect tombstone remnants after partial-eviction.
sara: Are these the cases where a prefix gets evicted mid-session but later requests reconstruct the prefix differently? that can leave stale fragments that prevent coalescing :grimacing: 
leah: Yup. We also noticed cross-variant rollouts cause key-serialization drift — same logical prefix serializes differently (ordering of metadata fields changed) so the new requests miss and the old fragments just linger.
mattj: quick sketch of the current key: `sha256(tenant_id || prefix_serialization)` — fragile across proto changes. Thinking of adding a tiny epoch byte and an explicit tombstone marker in page headers. e.g.
```
// key = sha256(tenant_id || epoch_byte || prefix_digest)
let epoch = config.prefix_epoch || 0;
let key = sha256(tenant_id + String.fromCharCode(epoch) + prefix_digest);
```
leah: Nice — epoch makes rollouts deterministic namespace bumps instead of leaving interleaved fragments. But that alone won't stop long-session growth when sessions generate many unique prefixes over time.
nicole: Proposal: per-session sliding retention + background compaction. Keep last-N prefixes per session (N default 12), mark older prefixes for asynchronous compaction, and run a page-level compactor that skips live prefixes and rewrites pages to remove tombstones. Simulated workload: cap=12 + compactor interval=5k tokens.
sara: Any perf numbers for that sim?
leah: Ran a microbench on canary: hit-rate +7% at 95th pct, p99 latency down ~12% for chat-heavy traces, and overall kv memory plateaued instead of linear drift. memcpy syscalls dropped noticeably (less page churn).
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for cluster-a with feature flag `kv.prefix_epoch=false` toggled off -> awaiting opt-in to avoid immediate namespace bump.
mattj: Next steps I want to land: (1) key epoch byte + proto compat layer, (2) page header tombstone counter + compactor trigger, (3) per-session retention cap and telemetry for 'ghost_prefix' counts, (4) add unit+integration tests that simulate cross-variant rollouts and long chat sessions. I'll open PRs for each piece with microbench artifacts.
sara: please include a stress test that alternates small serialization changes (e.g., toggling optional meta fields) to reproduce stale fragments. add histogram of prefix-lifetimes to monitoring.
nicole: also add a quick experiment to test prefix grouping: hash-prefix into M buckets and LRU evict at bucket granularity — might reduce fragmentation from many small prefixes.
mattj: Agreed. I'll include the bucketed-LRU as an optional lab flag so we can A/B.
leah: ETA for proto + tests: EOW if no surprises. I'll help with compactor perf tuning.

(annotations: :mag: profiler snapshots attached in thread; slack reactions: :thumbsup: on the microbench result)
